govt_response.summary: The Ministry of Power reported that electrification works in 99,470 villages had been completed and 1,73,79,364 BPL households connected as of 31 October 2011.

analysis:
The National Common Minimum Programme committed the UPA government to completing household electrification in five years, by 2009. The RGGVY target was 1,25,000 un-electrified villages and 7.8 crore rural households, including free connections for 2.34 crore BPL households.

By May 2014, about 1.05 lakh of the 1.25 lakh villages that were un-electrified in 2005 had been electrified. The Indian Express reported 18,542 villages still un-electrified on 1 April 2015.

The CAG's 2013 performance audit set out the 2009 target. The government's own 2011 release reported 99,470 villages covered and a revised Bharat Nirman target of 1 lakh villages by March 2012, which also slipped.
notes: The PMO speech page timed out during research; the BBC report and CAG audit were used for the promise and target. Village electrification is defined by the 2006 policy as basic infrastructure plus 10% household connections, not universal household access.
